A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaDA-MedV and provide complete, readable main text and Appendices A-B. Equations, tables, figures, and examples can be matched despite relocation and formatting changes.

before.justification: Tables 1-5 report original model evaluations and training/inference analyses. Appendix B includes generated-response examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, timing measurements, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same architecture, masked-prediction objective, three-stage training pipeline, low-confidence remasking, and semi-autoregressive inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same biomedical alignment/dialogue training data, open-ended conversation benchmark, VQA-RAD, English SLAKE, and PathVQA. The relocated VQA examples introduce no new evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1-4, including the nine conversation baselines, downstream VQA comparators, and LLaVA-Med200 prompt control. Table 7 retains the same model variants.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, training configurations, and generation settings remain unchanged in Section 5.1 and Tables 6 and 8. Section 5.2 expands the scoring description without establishing a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The initialization and fine-tuning comparisons, generation-length/sampling-step/block-length analyses, and qualitative cases are retained. v1 Figure 8 becomes v2 Figure 3; this is an existing case study, not an added analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and generated-response examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains the overall score of 52.605, and Table 2 retains closed-form accuracies of 84.93%, 92.31%, and 95.15%. Tables 3-5 also retain their results.

T1.justification: Equations 1-4 retain the same forward/reverse diffusion definitions and training objectives. Neither version adds or revises a formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claim, benchmark-performance claims, response-length controllability contribution, and training/inference findings.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 adds a favorable interpretation of the existing VQA examples, describing answers as correct and more informative and highlighting the peritoneum example's explanation. The limitations concerning open-form answers, computational cost, and token repetition remain.

D1.justification: v2 Section 5.2 explicitly documents averaging scores within question types and domains before reference normalization. v1 Appendix A.3 already described the judge, scoring criteria, and normalization, but not this aggregation order. Hardware, hyperparameters, and code/model access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 60 works and retain the same research positioning. References 51 and 52 exchange numbering, while other bibliographic edits concern formatting or metadata.

P1.justification: Section 5.2 is expanded and incorporates the evaluator footnote into the main discussion; Section 5.3 gains a short case interpretation. The redundant appendix VQA subsection is removed, the following subsection is renumbered, and an author affiliation is added.

P2.justification: v1 Appendix Figure 8 moves into the main text as v2 Figure 3 with a revised caption identifying question types and generation settings. Other figures are renumbered or repositioned, and table rules, sizing, and page layout receive limited formatting changes.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves evaluation transparency by specifying score aggregation in Section 5.2 and makes existing VQA examples accessible beside the main results. The scientific evidence is unchanged, and the more favorable case interpretation adds no validation, so the improvement is limited to clearer documentation and presentation.
